coordinate_frame: Selenographic planetocentric, Mean Earth/Polar Axis, longitude east-positive, [-180, 180)
selection_method: Each mission candidate is a published, individually traced coordinate inside one of the task's three candidate regions (Shackleton crater rim, the Shackleton-de Gerlache Connecting Ridge, de Gerlache crater rim). Primary provenance: LOLA illumination study of Mazarico et al. (2011), which the PGDA 5 m/pix site DEMs are named after; elevations are sampled from those DEMs. See docs/SITES.md for the full deliverable table and source notes.
disclaimer: Coordinates are exact published study points, not official Artemis landing-region definitions and not landing-certified sites. Sites 001/011 and 007 lie inside Artemis III candidate regions named by NASA in 2022; the Shackleton-rim point traces to the NASA 2020 crewed candidate list. Elevations are LOLA samples at the points, not terrain-averages. Verify against the IAU Gazetteer and LROC QuickMap before operational use.
mission_note: The A/B/C order of the mission candidates lives in config/lunanav.config.json -> mission.candidate_sites, not here. mission_candidates below must match it, and the backend refuses to load a catalogue that disagrees. elevation_m, slope_deg and nearest_psr are Task 1 records from LOLA and the LROC PSR catalogue - see docs/SITES.md.

sites.name: Shackleton Crater Rim (SR1)
sites.region: Rim of Shackleton crater (20.9 km diameter, IAU centre -89.67, 129.78E; the south pole lies on this rim)
sites.description: Sunlit crest on the rim of Shackleton crater, 10.5 km from the pole. The crater floor below is one of the largest, oldest PSRs at the pole (~40 K, possible surface ice), while the rim crest sees sunlight most of the year. The far-side-facing geometry keeps Earth low on the horizon, trading direct-to-Earth time for illumination.
sites.coordinate_note: Mazarico et al. (2011) LOLA point 4, cross-referenced to NASA 2020 crewed candidate site 004 (Kumari et al. 2022 / JESA Table 1); Glaser et al. (2017) independently place a rim cluster at -89.7815, 204.70E (1.4 km away, 82.1% mean illumination, 89.8% solar visibility, 65 h max shadow).
sites.source: Mazarico et al. 2011, Icarus 211, 1066 (point 4); NASA 2020 site 004

sources.label: Mazarico et al. 2011, Icarus 211, 1066-1081 (LOLA point 4, ~86.7% sunlit rate)

sites.elevation_note: LOLA 5 m/pix PGDA site DEM (Site04), median of the 125 m window at the point; height relative to the 1737.4 km reference sphere, RMS height uncertainty 0.32 m (Barker et al. 2021).

sites.name: Shackleton-de Gerlache Connecting Ridge (CR1)
sites.region: Ridge crest between Shackleton and de Gerlache craters (Artemis III candidate region 'Connecting Ridge', 2022)
sites.description: 16.7 km from the pole on the crest of the ridge linking Shackleton and de Gerlache. The best-lit ground documented at the south pole: Glaser et al. (2017) find 88.0% mean illumination and 92.1% solar visibility at 2 m on this crest, with darkness spells limited to a few days, and a 5,200 m2 PSR only ~100 m from the lit cluster. Like the Shackleton rim it faces the far side, so Earth sits low.
sites.coordinate_note: Mazarico et al. (2011) LOLA point 1, cross-referenced to NASA 2020 crewed candidate site 001; ESA/DLR studies of the same crest use CR1 at -89.4649, 222.1027E (De Rosa et al. 2012; Glaser et al. 2014); Glaser et al. (2017) C1 is at -89.4398, 222.83E, 1.9 km along the crest.
sites.source: Mazarico et al. 2011, Icarus 211, 1066 (point 1); NASA 2020 site 001

sites.name: de Gerlache Crater Rim (GR1)
sites.region: Rim of de Gerlache crater (32.7 km diameter, IAU centre -88.48, -88.34; Artemis III candidate region 'de Gerlache Rim 1', 2022)
sites.description: On the Earth-facing side of the pole: the counterpart geometry case where direct-to-Earth line of sight is favoured over illumination. Kumari et al. (2022) find the rim's central point is 82.6% illuminated on average, the rim crest rises ~1400 m, and a large old PSR on the crater floor holds trapped volatiles but is not safely reachable from the rim (walls steeper than 25 deg).
sites.coordinate_note: Mazarico et al. (2011) LOLA point 11, cross-referenced to NASA 2020 crewed candidate site 011; the same point is the central point analysed by Kumari et al. (2022) (max mean illumination 82.6%).
sites.source: Mazarico et al. 2011, Icarus 211, 1066 (point 11); NASA 2020 site 011

sites.name: Peak Near Shackleton (site 007)
sites.region: Massif between Shackleton and Slater craters (Artemis III candidate region 'Peak Near Shackleton', 2022)
sites.description: High-standing massif ~15 km from the Shackleton rim crest. Kumari et al. (2022) analyse this point in depth: 85.9% maximum mean illumination at the central point, slopes mostly <15 deg, small young PSRs within the site, and a water-detection PSR within the 10 km exploration zone.
sites.coordinate_note: Mazarico et al. (2011) LOLA point 7, cross-referenced to NASA 2020 crewed candidate site 007 (Kumari et al. 2022 / JESA Table 1). Reference site; not a Phase 1 mission candidate (the Shackleton-rim candidate covers this side of the pole).

sites.name: Malapert Massif
sites.description: Large massif near the 0 meridian, facing Earth; a candidate for steadier direct-to-Earth line of sight than sites on the far-side-facing slopes.
sites.coordinate_note: Approximate summit area; Mazarico et al. (2011) point 23 ('summit of Mt. Malapert') lies 1.4 km away at -85.97, 357.70E. Verify before use.

sites.name: Mons Mouton
sites.description: Flat-topped mountain (formerly Leibnitz beta); the IM-2 lander targeted its plateau in 2025.
sites.coordinate_note: Highest point per Wikipedia (84 deg 36' S 31 deg 00' E); Mazarico et al. (2011) point 20 (Leibnitz beta plateau) is at -85.43, 31.73E, ~93 km farther south.
